official_measurement_examples.name: Part O scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document O applies to new residential buildings in England and sets guidance for reducing overheating risk.

official_measurement_examples.name: Extensions exclusion
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current GOV.UK FAQ states Part O does not apply to extensions or conservatories added to residential buildings after they are built.

official_measurement_examples.name: Change-of-use exclusion
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current GOV.UK FAQ states Part O does not apply merely because a building undergoes a change of use.

official_measurement_examples.name: Two compliance methods
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current guidance recognises the simplified method and dynamic thermal modelling as two routes for demonstrating Part O compliance.

official_measurement_examples.name: TM59 evidence
official_measurement_examples.fact: For the dynamic method, GOV.UK FAQ says the building control body should receive a report demonstrating the residential building passes the relevant TM59 assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Mechanical cooling interaction
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK FAQ says mechanical cooling used to pass Part O must be reflected in Part L calculations.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2022 commencement baseline
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2021 amendment regulations introducing the overheating requirement came into force on 15 June 2022, with transitional provisions.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 consultation response status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Future Homes and Buildings Standards consultation page was updated 24 March 2026 and says relevant outcomes will be implemented through statutory instruments and new approved documents.

core_rules: Approved Document O compliance is not planning permission
planning permission is not Part O compliance
Part O applies to new residential buildings and must not be assumed for all building work
Part O does not apply to ordinary extensions to existing residential buildings
Part O does not apply to material change of use merely because residential occupation results
simplified method is distinct from dynamic thermal modelling
passing simplified method is not planning permission
passing dynamic thermal modelling is not planning permission
TM59 report is evidence for Building Regulations compliance not a planning decision
high-risk location classification is not a planning constraint designation
moderate-risk location classification is not proof of low parcel risk
glazing-area limit is not a planning density control
shading requirement is not planning permission
opening free-area requirement is not guaranteed usable ventilation
security constraints on openings require actual design evidence
noise constraints on openings require actual evidence and are not automatically resolved by Part O
pollution constraints on openings require actual evidence
mechanical cooling used for Part O must also be reflected in Part L assessment
mechanical cooling is not a planning permission
Part O compliance does not prove Part L compliance
Part L compliance does not prove Part O compliance
Approved Document O guidance is not the only possible compliance route
building-control acceptance is not planning permission
completion certificate is not planning permission
2021 consultation proposal is not current law
2021 government response is not itself the statutory instrument
2023 consultation call for evidence is not adopted Part O amendment
24 March 2026 consultation response is not itself an amended Approved Document O
future implementation statement must not be treated as commenced law without the instrument or revised document
15 June 2022 commencement must be preserved for current Part O baseline
transitional arrangements must be evidenced for the actual building
pre-commencement building notice does not automatically exempt all later phases
commencement of one building does not automatically transition every building on a multi-building site
correction circular is not a new planning permission
corrected Approved Document edition must be distinguished from superseded text
overheating risk assessment is not a climate-change planning permission
weather file selection is a modelling input not parcel climate certainty
future climate scenario is not a current legal threshold unless specified
solar gain control is not proof of daylight compliance
daylight assessment is distinct from Part O overheating compliance
ventilation strategy is not proof of air-quality compliance
Part O is distinct from Part F ventilation requirements
Part O is distinct from fire-safety requirements affecting openings
residential building scope must be evidenced and not inferred from planning description alone
source edition and transition dates must be preserved
NO_DATA must remain NO_DATA rather than no overheating constraint
no parcel overheating compliance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research confidence is not parcel Part O accuracy
